review_defects.where: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/run_context.rs:641-671 (persona_toggle future inside tokio::join!), via sse.rs load_thread_persona_enabled -> load_context_assembly_messages (sse.rs:4902-4907, no timeout)
review_defects.scenario: Set MODEL_GATEWAY_RUN_CONTEXT to instructions or full. The BFF always injects persona_instructions for a user who has a persona, so the persona read runs. The read is session-core GetContextAssembly, and it has no per-request bound: the channel only has a 5 s connect timeout, and the session-core handler does DB reads and memory-bucket loading, including Letta. If that RPC stalls (a slow DB or Letta, or a wedged replica), tokio::join! waits on it no matter how fast the 3 s HISTORY_TIMEOUT and 400 ms memory futures finish. The Do run then sits prepared and never dispatched, and the client sees only `connected` for as long as the RPC hangs. The module claims 'a slow store must cost the history, not the run' and 'None of them can fail the run', but one unbounded read defeats both claims. This also happens in `instructions` mode, which the plan names as the first and safest staging step.
review_defects.fix: Wrap the persona read in tokio::time::timeout with its own short bound (for example the same 3 s as HISTORY_TIMEOUT, or less). On elapse, fall back to `true`, which is the same fail-open default the function already uses on error. Add a unit/e2e test with a session-core mock whose get_context_assembly never returns, and assert that the run still dispatches within the bound.

review_defects.scenario: A thread whose prior turns exceed MODEL_GATEWAY_RUN_CONTEXT_HISTORY_TOKENS is cut by the token-budget planner (apply_head_drop), not by the contract caps. The run record still stamps history {state: truncated, reason: "cap"}. An operator reading runs.metadata.run_context therefore cannot tell 'cut by the configured budget' from 'cut by the executor's hard 24-message/64 KiB cap'. Those two need different remediations (raise the env budget, or accept that the contract cap is the limit). The status is the only audit trail of what a run was told, so this mislabels it. 'cap' is also not in the plan's closed-reason list, and the plan's `waived_default` is never emitted.

notes:
What was built. run_context.rs holds RunContextMode (strict parse: only the exact lowercase literals "instructions" and "full" enable; anything else is off), the history-token budget (default 8000, clamp 1000-40000), AuthoredLayers, the single compose_authored_instructions that both Ask and Do now use (sse.rs authored_instructions_message is a thin wrapper, output unchanged), bound_history, the pure compose(), the async prepare() and record_status(). prepare() reads the persona toggle (only when persona text exists and the run is not ZDR), the thread history (3 s bound) and memory (the Ask 400 ms budget) concurrently, composes, logs closed tokens and counts only, and stamps RecordRunContext best-effort (2 s bound). compaction.rs gains apply_head_drop, run_history_dropped_notice and RUN_HISTORY_DROPPED_NOTICE. sse.rs threads Option<RunContext> through spawn_run_dispatch, resolved_run_agent_request and build_run_agent_request; agentic_run_stream takes Option<RunContextRequest> as a last parameter, composes right after the connected frame and never for a continuation; invoke_stream_sse builds the request (none when the switch is off, and the layers are not even read); continue_run passes None.

Behaviour. Off: no field, no extra read, no RecordRunContext call (e2e proves byte-identical request for unset, off, FULL, true, 1, instruction). Instructions: authored text only; history and memory stay unstated on the record. Full: also bounded history and memory. The pinned subscription route gets instructions only (history and memory stamped skipped_by_policy/route_uncached). Memory is skipped, stamped skipped_by_policy, for a trivial prompt (reason trivial_prompt) and for a Space-scoped run (space_scope). ZDR: instructions allowed, history and memory skipped with reason zdr, status never recorded. Waived: composed like an Ask turn (DEC-32 default) but the status is not recorded because session-core refuses a waived credential. Timeout, error and missing credential make the part UNAVAILABLE with that closed reason, never EMPTY. The current user turn (the thread's last user message, persisted before dispatch) is dropped from history. History is cut with plan_head_summary_by_budget plus apply_head_drop, then to the contract caps (24 messages, 64 KiB) so execution-core's validate can never refuse a composed run; an oversize authored text is truncated and stated (truncated/cap) rather than refused. The e2e test asserts that apart from run_context the full-mode request equals the off request (mode, rung, plan_mode, budget unchanged).

Deviations. (1) The switch is read from the environment once per dispatched run (RunContextMode::from_env in invoke_stream_sse), not in a process-wide OnceLock: the e2e suite flips switches per test with serial EnvGuard, which a latched OnceLock would break; rollback is still unset/off plus restart. (2) fetch_chat_memory_context is left byte-for-byte as it was, because memory_prefetch.rs (not mine) has a source-reading test that counts its early returns; the run reads memory through run_context::load_memory (same request, same timeout constant made pub(crate), same outcome metric made pub(crate)), because the Ask function folds timeout/error/empty into one empty answer and the run record must tell them apart. (3) Instead of making load_context_assembly_messages pub(crate) (its return type is private), sse.rs gets pub(crate) load_thread_persona_enabled, which delegates to it with no Data Plane bearer so no retrieval is paid. (4) The closed reason waived_default is not stamped anywhere: a waived run is composed like Ask and its status is not recorded; if the owner wants waived Do runs to skip history and memory, it is a one-line change in plan_history. (5) The notice left where history was cut is an assistant turn that names no recovery tool (the Do loop has no reattach_context, and a run's history may carry only user/assistant roles per mp_contracts::run_context::validate). (6) Eval case 16 requires the fixtures authored-instruction-fixture and run-context-instructions: the eval harness calls model-gateway directly, so the BFF-injected org/Space/persona layers never reach it; the case exercises the deployment's PLATFORM_SYSTEM_INSTRUCTIONS layer (sentinel EVAL-RULE-7) and says so in its header. Case 15 requires run-context-full. Both skip honestly until EVAL_CAPABILITIES names them. test_runner.py: count 14 to 16, the 12-seed-turn threshold now applies only to cases tagged compaction, plus one new test for the run-context cases.

shared-edit apps/Model Plane/docs/decisions/ledger.md: insert the four entries below directly under the '---' separator, above '## 2026-10-21 - The reasoning-effort ladder lives in inference-core (WS11-S1)', each followed by one blank line.

## 2026-10-21 - Tool side-effect classes are declared in the registry; the name heuristics are the oracle until then (WS05)

**Status: proposed.** Today the permission gate infers risk from the tool name. `permission::is_risky_tool` matches a fixed list of destructive and outbound verbs as substrings, and every `mcp__` name is risky. `rung_required_for` and `check_autonomy_rung` take the rung from that same match, and the only argument-level refinement is `execute_provider_action`, by its catalogued operation. A name cannot say what a tool does, so an unlisted or renamed tool gets whatever substring it happens to contain. The proposal: each offered tool would carry a declared side-effect class (`read`, `sandbox_compute`, `context_write`, `external_write`, `destructive`, `owner_effect`, with `unclassified` as the strictest default) and an approval floor, held in capability-core's per-tool registry and carried in the signed policy decision; execution-core would decide from the class. The name lists are deleted only after a shadow comparison shows zero built-in divergence. Until then `legacy_classification_golden` in `permission/mod.rs` pins what the heuristics answer for every offered name and the MCP spellings, and the class-derived answers must reproduce it for every built-in. Plan: `docs/plans/model-plane-chat-build-plan-2026-10-14.md`, WS05.

## 2026-10-21 - A declared class may tighten a tool but never loosen a seeded row (WS05)

**Status: proposed.** A class that comes from outside the seed (an MCP server's `readOnlyHint`, a registrant's form, a generic registry upsert) may raise a tool's class or add an approval floor. It may not lower the class of a row the seed already classed without the override scope that protects a high risk level today. `enforceRiskFloor` in capability-core already refuses a plain write that would lower a currently high capability, and it fails closed for the seeded high-risk ids; the proposal applies that rule to the per-tool class. An MCP annotation is a third-party claim: it is untrusted by default, a read-only hint would derive `external_write`, and a tool whose description or schema changes after its first observation would be disabled until a person re-approves it. Relaxation is a separate decision: a user or org `allow` would apply only to a digest-pinned MCP row, never to a built-in, an `owner_effect` tool or an `unclassified` one (plan WS05 D6, DEC-08; the relaxation lands in WS05-S5).

## 2026-10-21 - The MCP observation write is an org-scoped internal route that can only create or refresh observations (WS05 D5)

**Status: proposed; needs a security sign-off before WS05-S2 merges.** To observe MCP tools (WS05-S2), model-gateway would post tool digests and hints to capability-core over the org-derived internal route, authenticated by the `X-Mcp-Service-Token` that the internal MCP routes already check (`registry_apis.go`). The route would create or refresh observation rows and nothing else: it cannot approve a drifted tool, lower a class or write policy. A ZDR caller never writes an observation, and an observation carries digests, classes and hints, never descriptions, schemas, arguments or outputs. Rejected alternatives: a user bearer (a read-only user could not write the observation) and a Control-issued principal (a new entry in a Control-owned file, before the narrow route is shown to be insufficient). Any change that lets this route do more reopens this entry. It is not the service identity the Verevon relay ruling rejects: the route is scoped to one org, stores only digests and hints, and returns no tenant content.

## 2026-10-21 - Non-read MCP tools are withheld from Do runs until an approved call can be resumed (WS05 D3)

**Status: deferred.** An approved MCP call cannot be resumed cold. The approval delivery worker resumes only `execute_provider_action`, `book_shipment` and `tickets.create`, and its module doc says arbitrary MCP tools have unknown, third-party idempotency semantics, so an `ask` pause on an MCP write would be recorded and then never run. Until a continuation can execute an approved MCP call exactly once, the only MCP mode that may be enabled is `MCP_DO_TOOLS=read`: it would offer and execute read-class MCP tools only, and `all` stays blocked. Revisit when the in-place resume (WS03) and resumable approvals (WS13) run an approved MCP call once on a rebuilt stack. The trigger is that proof, not a date.
